decision: OBSERVATION_UNAVAILABLE; business recovery is not established by the timeout
facts: The recorded screenshot attempts timed out or returned a busy rejection while title and URL reads remained responsive.
No screenshot image was obtained during the failure window.
The failure record classifies the event as an environment tool failure and records the tab as alive.
The caller-side contract separates observation failure from action failure and permits a new capture surface only when an independent liveness probe proves the page dead.
A later observation record preserves an UNKNOWN presentation position and records no pending business action at that wedge.
inferences: The timeout is evidence of an unavailable capture channel, not evidence that the page or a business action failed.
Because liveness was observed, opening a new surface, reloading the game, or resuming the produce is not an automatic consequence supported by this evidence.
Any later semantic state conclusion requires a fresh trustworthy observation and, where applicable, reconciliation against the durable state.
unknowns: The visual and semantic page state during the unavailable interval is unknown.
The exact mechanism of the browser transport stall is unknown.
The outcome of any business action that might have been in flight is unknown unless separately reconciled.
reason: A live tab with a failed screenshot channel supports only the OBSERVATION_UNAVAILABLE classification. The timeout does not establish page failure, action failure, or a basis for automatic business recovery.
